name: provenance_reassertion
description: After B becomes current, the older value A is re-quoted in a more recent turn — a user pasting an old message, a tool echoing a cached record, a summary repeating history. Re-quoting is not a mutation: B stays current unless the turn declares one. Paired with declared_mutation_accept_rate, because a store that never updates anything also never spuriously supersedes.

ops.human: Ship the release to the eu-west-1 region.
Change of plan, deploy target is eu-central-1.
For context, here's what I wrote last week: 'Ship the release to the eu-west-1 region.'
ops.notes: Verbatim re-quote of the superseded value in a newer turn. Must not become current.

ops.human: We renegotiated: the Northwind SLA is now 99.9%.

ops.notes: Stale tool output re-asserting A. Recency of the *message* is not recency of the *fact*.

ops.human: Handover done — Marcus is the incident commander now.
Recap of the timeline so far: Priya was paged at 02:10 and took over as incident commander.
ops.notes: Historical narration, not a mutation. The past tense is the signal.

ops.human: Revert the deploy target back to eu-west-1, eu-central-1 is capacity constrained.
ops.notes: An explicit revert to the old value. This one must be accepted: the battery is not rewarding immobility.

ops.human: Priya is back on as incident commander for the second shift.
ops.notes: Declared mutation restoring an earlier value. Accepting this and rejecting r3 is the whole skill being measured.

ops.human: Northwind renegotiated again — the SLA is 99.95% from next quarter.
ops.notes: Declared mutation to a value that has never been current before. The other two declared mutations revert to earlier values, which an immobile store passes by accident; this one it cannot.

ops.text: What is the current Northwind SLA?

ops.human: Copying the old thread for the postmortem: 'Handover done — Marcus is the incident commander now.'

assert.notes: Re-quote of the value that was current two states ago must not win either.
